# Landscape lenses — lightweight Canon RF

**Dimension:** lightweight wide and ultra-wide Canon-brand RF/RF-S lenses for
landscapes. Sources in [citations.md](../citations.md); terms in
[glossary](../glossary.md).

## Why wide lenses suit landscapes

Wide and ultra-wide focal lengths (≈10–35 mm full-frame-equivalent) capture a
broad sweep of a scene and exaggerate depth, making foregrounds feel large and
skies vast [[35]](../citations.md#c35). "Ultra-wide" is roughly anything below
24 mm equivalent.

## Recommendation logic

- **APS-C body:** the only native RF ultra-wide is the **RF-S 10-18mm** (~150 g,
  16–29 mm-equiv) — lightest option and the true ultra-wide for crop bodies
  [[32]](../citations.md#c32).
- **Full-frame body, budget:** **RF 15-30mm** (~390 g, has IS) is the best
  balance of range, weight, stabilization, and price
  [[33]](../citations.md#c33).
- **Full-frame, quality + weather:** **RF 14-35mm f/4L** is sharpest, sealed,
  takes 77 mm filters — but ~3× the price and 540 g [[34]](../citations.md#c34).

## Counter-perspectives

- **Ultra-wide is hard to compose** — without a strong foreground, beginners
  often find ultra-wide shots look empty/distorted [[31]](../citations.md#c31).
- **Slow apertures (f/6.3) limit low light** at golden/blue hour; the RF 16mm is
  faster (f/2.8) but has **no IS** to counter shake
  [[30]](../citations.md#c30)[[33]](../citations.md#c33).
- **A kit zoom may suffice:** the bundled RF-S 18-45mm reaches 29 mm-equiv —
  wide enough for many scenics — so a dedicated wide adds cost/weight a beginner
  may not exploit [[35]](../citations.md#c35).
- **APS-C limits true ultra-wide:** the 1.6× crop turns full-frame wides into
  normal lenses (RF 16mm → 26 mm), so APS-C buyers must use the RF-S 10-18mm for
  ultra-wide [[28]](../citations.md#c28)[[32]](../citations.md#c32).
- **Budget options aren't weather-sealed** — only the RF 14-35L is, and landscape
  shooting invites rain/dust/spray [[34]](../citations.md#c34).

## Gaps and limitations

- Weather sealing of the RF-S 10-18mm was not explicitly confirmed; treated as
  not sealed pending Canon spec confirmation [[32]](../citations.md#c32).
- Lens weights are review-site figures via snippets (Canon/spec pages blocked).
- The RF 24mm f/1.8 Macro (24 mm = wide but not ultra-wide) is covered under
  [macro-lenses](macro-lenses.md); it can double for wide scenes.
